reviews.review: Great game overall. The feelings of exploration and hazard exposure are very strong and pervasive. Totally a mystic experience. The dialogues are great. Characters are deep and relatable, even if overall only one or two crewmates out of ten are really enjoyable to spend time with exploring or chatting. The screenplay and the script are really good, though not greatly implemented (notably the main story ends in a stupidly abrupt way). Some animations are fascinating. Most concepts are owe inspiring. The colonization effort towards a new galaxy are the risks related to this pioneristic emprise is a great way to depart from the old storyline (which formibadly ended with the third installment of the series). Some bugs are really annoying (can't complete some map locations or the galaxy map). At the end of the game you could still end up with a quests (remnant data cores) which cannot be completed because you cannot go back to certain locations or try again story missions. Played 116 hours. 99% game completion because of the quest i couldn't complete.
very enjoyable and interesting to play need some more species and also some more planets to settle on

Lovely experience I would recommend after all is said and done.

Some negatives:
- The tone options in the dialogue wheel are great and a decent compromise for those who don't want to read or desire a more conversational pace, but the option to see the whole response needs to become a thing. 
- Exposition interrogations. Not always, but there were a few jarring ones.
- Formulaic and slightly repetitive gameplay when it comes to exploration and quest design.

Neutral:
- Slightly rushed, average plot (in particular the ending). Still better paced than ME1 and there were some great personal moments.
- Science fantasy (a matter of personal preference).

Some positives:
- Characterization was mostly very good, with some exceptions. Very much appreciated how 'human' the interactions between crew members and reactions to situations felt, something very few video games get right (which may also be a slight rebuke at the same time; the aliens and your interactions with them are way too human. I wasn't expecting Solaris, but we can find a middle ground. This is true of the ME franchise as a whole though, rather than a criticism solely directed at Andromeda).

- Mountains and mountains of great environmental dialogue between npcs, no matter how important or irrelevant they may be. Very impressive.

- Great combat. Occasional, completely optional jumping puzzles and other similar secrets.

- World and everything else in it looks beautiful. Sometimes random npcs don't really have much animation going on during dialogues, but not an issue.
